about: Hand-kept supplement to the procurement records (bom.json, catalog-en.json, cart-plan.json, sourcing-policy.json of the build pack). It names the parts the foundation robot carries that those records predate (the head board change of 2026-10-17, the touch board, the battery backpack, the soles) and marks records the foundation no longer uses. scripts/build_bom.py merges it into BOM.md.

pi.note: Raspberry Pi Zero W head board until 2026-10-17; replaced by the Radxa Cubie A7Z (D-011). Not on the robot.

camera.note: Camera Module 3 Wide was the Pi-era eye camera; replaced by the Radxa Camera 13M 214 on the A7Z CSI port (D-011).

camera_ffc.note: Pi camera ribbon; the Radxa camera comes with its own CSI cable.

pd_receiver.note: Power route A: the HUSB238 decoy that asks the USB-C PD source for 20 V (D-007, D-014). The 'retired 2026-10-13' flag in the record is stale.

shared_regulator.note: Power route B: makes 5 V for the A7Z inside the battery backpack (D-010). Bought; backpack not yet on the robot.

power_disconnect.note: XT30 pair: the robot's servo inlet for the battery backpack (D-010).

main_fuse.note: Bought for an earlier harness; the foundation harness carries no fuses (D-013).

audio_gain_resistor.note: The MAX98357A GAIN and SD pads are left open; the volume ceiling is the -3 dB ALSA softvol (D-012).

pi_mount_screws.note: Pi Zero W mount; the A7Z sits on the head cap rails with M2.6 x 6 (see the build guide).

pi_header_housing.note: Pi-era idea; every head wire is a single Dupont plug on the A7Z header.

pi_gpio_power.note: The two 5 V leads to A7Z header pins 2 and 6.

existing_usb_charger.note: Xiaomi 67 W charger of the 15 V era. The foundation runs from a 20 V 5 A USB-C PD charger or the Xiaomi 212W power bank (CURRENT-STATE power).

robotis_smps_12v.note: Kit accessory, not in either power route.

smps2dxl.note: Kit accessory, not in either power route.

smps2dxl_cable.note: Kit accessory, not in either power route.

sd.note: The 16 GB microSD now carries the A7Z Debian image (3-brain-and-senses).

sd_reader.note: Needed once to write the A7Z card.

additions.note: Head computer since 2026-10-17 (D-011). Ordered on Amazon 2026-10-15; the listing and price were not kept in the project records. Radxa product page: https://radxa.com/products/cubie/a7z

Eye camera on the A7Z CSI port, screwed to the V1.17 face panel bosses with four M2 x 4. Ordered on Amazon 2026-10-15; listing and price not kept. Radxa docs: https://docs.radxa.com/en/accessories/camera/camera-13m-214
Touch readout board in the head cap: five capacitive inputs, I2C slave at 0x2A to the A7Z (D-013). Price read 2026-10-15.

additions.model: Copper foil tape with conductive adhesive, 5 mm strips
additions.note: The five touch pads inside the head cap (L1, R1 18 mm; L2, R2, M 12 mm). Price from the touch plan (USD 5.95); listing not kept.

additions.model: Tattu 650 mAh 2S 7.4 V 75C LiPo, XT30 plug
additions.note: Power route B (D-010). Bought 2026-10; backpack not yet on the robot.

additions.model: Tenergy LiPo safety bag, medium 7 x 9 in
additions.note: Charging and storage bag for the two packs.

additions.model: Amass XT30U male + female, 10 pairs with heat shrink
additions.note: Backpack feed lead (male) and servo lead (female); spares.
The 5 V joint for the A7Z lead: a shape that cannot mate with the XT30 servo joint.

additions.model: Swann 39 rocker switch (RoboClub drawer); D-010 planned the REV-31-1387 XT30 switch
additions.note: The V1.20 and V1.31 backpack frames carry the 12.3 x 27.5 mm cutout for the Swann 39 body.

additions.model: USB-C PD wall charger with a 20 V 5 A (100 W) PDO
additions.note: Power route A source. A 20 V 3 A (60 W) charger folds back at the walking current peaks and freezes the A7Z (2026-10-22). Model not recorded.
Power route A source for untethered runs; the robot ran from it on 2026-10-23.

additions.model: XL4015 CC/CV buck converter modules (two, from the ROBOTIS OMX-AI kits)
additions.note: #1 makes the servo rail, #2 the A7Z 5 V, both in the rear converter box (D-007).

additions.model: ROBOTIS OMX-AI kit (two kits supply the 15 XL330-M288-T, the OpenRB-150, the X3P cables, the XL4015 modules and the TAP screws)
additions.note: The servo and controller rows below are allocated from these kits; the kit price is not kept in the records.

additions.model: Radxa AC019 dual-band FPC Wi-Fi antenna, IPEX gen 1, 42 x 11.9 mm
additions.note: Stuck under the front of the head cap crown (docs/A7Z-ANTENNA.html).

additions.model: Discarded bicycle inner tube (butyl, about 1 mm) plus thin double-sided tape
additions.note: Foot soles, cut with the template in the feet-sole study; the hot-glue mold route was dropped 2026-10-19.
